record.paper_title: Towards Knowledge Exchange: State-of-the-Art and Open Problems
record.original_question: How can execution of transformation queries produced by knowledge-base mapping generation tools be optimized when the generated SPARQL queries contain many nested OPTIONAL clauses, which are required for open-world knowledge-base integration tasks but are expensive because query engines often process them as left outer joins?

evidence.quote: We believe our approach (as well as many other KB integration approaches) can immensely benefit from research on how to optimize the execution of queries that use SPARQL OPTIONAL clauses.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider SPARQL, the standard query language for RDF graphs. A basic graph pattern (BGP) is a finite set of triple patterns of the form (s, p, o) in which each component is either an IRI/literal or a variable. The OPTIONAL operator combines two patterns P1 and P2 into a pattern (P1 OPT P2) whose evaluation over an RDF graph G is the left outer join of the evaluations of P1 and P2: every solution of P1 is preserved, extended by a compatible solution of P2 when one exists. SPARQL queries with arbitrarily nested OPTIONAL patterns are known to have PSPACE-complete evaluation in general, and queries built from BGPs and OPT only (well-designed or not) are typically executed by query engines using a left-outer-join physical plan.

In knowledge-base integration and ontology-based data-access scenarios, automatically generated transformation queries that materialize mappings from heterogeneous sources into a target schema routinely produce SPARQL queries that contain many deeply nested OPTIONAL clauses, since attributes in the source may or may not exist for each entity (open-world assumption). The cost of evaluating such queries via left outer joins grows rapidly with the depth and number of OPT operators, because left outer joins admit only restricted reordering and force the engine to retain unmatched tuples padded with nulls.

Problem. Develop a query-evaluation algorithm (with proofs of correctness with respect to the standard SPARQL set/bag semantics) for SPARQL queries of the form

   Q ::= BGP | (Q OPT Q) | (Q AND Q) | (Q FILTER F)

such that, for queries with n triple patterns and k nested OPTIONAL operators, the worst-case evaluation cost on an RDF graph with m triples is asymptotically strictly better than the cost obtained by treating every OPT as a generic left outer join in a relational engine. Specifically: identify a syntactic or semantic subclass of SPARQL OPTIONAL queries that captures the patterns arising from automatic knowledge-base mapping generation, give a sound and complete evaluation procedure for this subclass whose complexity is polynomial in m and n (and ideally independent of k beyond a low-degree polynomial), and prove matching lower bounds showing that no further asymptotic improvement is possible within the subclass.
artifact.status_search_result: Optimization of nested SPARQL OPTIONAL queries remains an active research topic. Several partial approaches exist (OptBitMat, Left Bit Right, the Nested Optional Join operator, and various SQL-translation techniques), each improving on naive left-outer-join evaluation for specific subclasses, but no general optimal algorithm for arbitrary nested OPTIONAL patterns is known and the evaluation problem is PSPACE-complete in general, so the problem is considered open in its full generality.

status_evidence.title: Left Bit Right: For SPARQL Join Queries with OPTIONAL Patterns
status_evidence.snippet: Optimization of OPTIONAL pattern queries (a.k.a. SQL left-outer-joins) poses additional challenges due to the restrictions on the reordering of left-outer-joins.
status_evidence.claim: Nested OPTIONAL optimization is acknowledged as an open challenge with only partial solutions.

status_evidence.title: Relational Nested Optional Join for Efficient Semantic Web Query Processing
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes a nested optional join (NOJ) operator more efficient than left outer join for nested optional graph patterns.
status_evidence.claim: Specialized operators have been proposed but a general optimal solution is not established.

status_evidence.title: A technique for SPARQL OPTIONAL (left-outer-join) queries
status_evidence.snippet: OptBitMat aggressively prunes candidate RDF triples for nested OPTIONAL and BGP queries.
status_evidence.claim: Active ongoing research with partial techniques rather than a definitive solution.
